0.0.n: Introduces the first point in the explanation.

0.2.n: The name of a prefecture in Japan.

0.3.n: Marks the location where the hot spring exists.

0.4.n: Makes Ehime the topic, attaching to に rather than replacing it.

0.5.n: A country name; 日本で sets the area for the comparison.

0.6.n: Sets the scope of the comparison: among hot springs in Japan.

0.7.n: Placed before 古い to make it mean oldest.

0.8.n: Describes the hot spring's age; 一番 makes this a comparison with all others.

0.9.n: Marks 日本で一番古い as the content of what people say.

0.10.n: 言う becomes passive 言われる, then 言われている, presenting a generally repeated claim.

0.11.n: The description before it identifies which kind of hot spring is being introduced.

0.12.n: Identifies 温泉 as the thing that exists.

0.13.n: The polite form of ある, used for the existence of things rather than people or animals.

1.0.n: 年 counts years; together with 前, this locates a time in the past.

1.1.n: Follows a length of time to indicate how far back something was.

1.2.n: Marks 3,000 years ago as the starting point of the hot spring's existence.

1.3.n: The plain form of ある; with a past starting point and から, it describes existence continuing to now.

1.4.n: Marks the preceding statement as what people say.

1.5.n: The polite version of 言われている; the passive form leaves the people making the claim unnamed.

2.0.n: A place name forming the first part of the hot spring's name.

2.1.n: Here it forms part of the proper name 道後温泉, commonly written Dogo Onsen in English.

2.2.n: Marks 道後温泉 as the name used with 言います.

2.3.n: The polite form of 言う; with a name followed by と, it tells us what something is called.

0.lit: First, in Ehime, there is a hot spring said to be the oldest in Japan.
0.tip: Everything from 日本で through 言われている describes the noun 温泉 that follows.

1.lit: It is said that it exists since 3,000 years ago.
1.tip: 前から means since a point in the past, linking that starting point to the present.

2.tip: Name + と言います is a standard way to tell someone what something is called.
